target_customer: Homeowners who wanted a professional interior decorator at a fraction of traditional design fees
problem: Hiring an interior decorator was expensive, with fees the TechCrunch launch article puts at starting around 5,000 dollars, and hard to arrange. Tastemaker matched customers with vetted decorators at flat prices and sold the furnishings.
business_model: Marketplace taking a cut of design fees plus online furniture retail

founders.name: Joe Fraiman
founders.background_notes: No background found in opened sources.

founders.name: Esther Park Hallam
founders.background_notes: Shown as Esther Park in a Business of Home result.

competitors.name: Scoutzie
competitors.what: Y Combinator startup with a similar request for proposals model connecting customers to designers

competitors.name: Houzz
competitors.what: Home design platform described by TechCrunch as more project focused and democratic

technical_complexity.rationale: A matching and commerce marketplace with a photo upload flow; standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Supply of decorators and demand from homeowners could be replicated, and several e-design startups launched around the same time.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent buying or copying Tastemaker. Many later e-design startups such as Modsy and Laurel and Wolf shut down, which shows a hard category.

market_need_then: Traditional designer fees started in the thousands of dollars, while Tastemaker priced design plans at about 600 to 2,250 dollars depending on room size (TechCrunch, August 2012).

branding.domain_note: Company site is tastemaker.com per the YC page.

identity.voice_and_tone: The April 2013 launch release was titled about decorating without the drama, a light consumer tone.

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch at launch and by Dwell and Business of Home; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Some trade and tech press at launch, a registered word mark, but no evidence of recall. The name is a common phrase used by many other businesses.

outcome_analysis: Tastemaker launched in closed beta in August 2012 and publicly in April 2013 and raised about 1.6 million dollars from Crosslink Capital and Y Combinator according to CB Insights. The YC directory marks it Inactive with no date, and no shutdown report, post-mortem or acquisition was found, so the cause is not public. Similar e-design startups later collapsed, but no source ties that to Tastemaker.
notes: The seed round rests on a single database (CB Insights, seen only in a search summary, undated; it said about 13 years ago). Company site tastemaker.com returned no usable content. The April 2013 public launch date comes from a press release seen only in a search summary. CB Insights page itself returned HTTP 403. The press release page for details was rate limited. Founder education and employers were not found.
